renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  title: Mean genome coverage per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library: its mean read depth over the reference, as reported by Qualimap BamQC. It answers how deeply each library covers the genome and whether the libraries are comparable.
    How to read: bars of similar height mean an even sequencing effort. A very short bar is a library that will give few usable calls, so compare it with the percentage of reads mapped and the duplication rate in the table before deciding to resequence it.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median mean depth of a library of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Qualimap, which draws no pass level.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: mean_coverage
    color: sample
    labels:
      sample: Library
      mean_coverage: Mean depth (X)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: mean_coverage

- component: card
  title: Mean depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average of the per-library mean depth, and the bars rank the deepest libraries. It answers how much sequencing the run holds per base of the reference.
    How to read: a large gap between the highest and the lowest library means an unbalanced run. Open the coverage histogram to see whether a low mean hides a covered fraction that is still adequate.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  column: mean_coverage
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: average over libraries, with the deepest ones ranked
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Duplication rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average percent of reads Qualimap estimates as duplicated, and the box shows how libraries spread around it. It answers whether the libraries lost much of their depth to duplicates.
    How to read: a library far above the box is over-amplified or low in input DNA, so its effective depth is lower than the mean depth suggests. The estimate is Qualimap's own and is not a pass or fail verdict.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  column: duplication_rate
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: average percent duplicated, with its spread

- component: card
  title: GC content
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average GC percentage of the mapped reads, and the bars rank the libraries with the highest value. It answers whether the libraries share a base composition.
    How to read: libraries of the same species and protocol should sit close together. An outlier suggests contamination, a different library preparation or a GC bias in amplification.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  column: gc_percentage
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: average percent GC, with the highest libraries ranked

- component: table
  title: BamQC summary per library
  description: |-
    Each row is a library with its read counts, share of reads mapped, mean depth, mean mapping quality, error rate, GC content and duplication rate. It answers the exact value behind every other tile of this output.
    How to read: sort by mean depth or by duplication rate to find the libraries that need attention, then compare them with the coverage tiles.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html

- component: advanced_viz
  id: reference_coverage_track
  title: Read depth along the reference
  description: |-
    Each point is a window of the reference, drawn at its position on its contig with the read depth Qualimap measured there, one line per library. It answers where along the genome the reads pile up or thin out.
    How to read: a flat line means an even library. Spikes point to repeats, amplified regions or organelle contigs, and long gaps point to regions the reads do not reach. Compare libraries to separate a sample effect from a reference effect.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  kind: coverage_track
  config:
    color_by: sample
  roles:
    chromosome: chromosome
    position: position
    value: coverage
    sample: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: reference_genome_view
  title: Read depth on the genome axis
  description: |-
    Each point is a window of the reference with its read depth, laid out on a chromosome-aware axis that can be zoomed. It answers the same question as the coverage track with a scrollable view of every contig.
    How to read: zoom into a region where the depth departs from its neighbours and compare libraries. Qualimap defines no depth cut-off, so no threshold line is drawn.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  kind: genome_view
  config:
    score_title: Read depth (X)
  roles:
    chr: chromosome
    pos: position
    score: coverage
    sample: sample

- component: figure
  title: Depth along the concatenated reference
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: the read depth in every window, with all contigs laid end to end on one axis. It answers how the depth profiles of the libraries compare along the whole reference.
    How to read: parallel lines mean the libraries react to the reference in the same way. A library whose line departs from the others at the same positions points to a library-specific bias.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: global_position
    y: coverage
    color: sample
    labels:
      global_position: Position on the concatenated reference (bp)
      coverage: Read depth (X)
      sample: Library

- component: card
  title: Window depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average read depth over all windows and libraries, and the box shows how the windows spread. It answers how even the depth is across the reference.
    How to read: a box that is narrow and close to the average means an even library. A long upper whisker means a few windows soak up many reads.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  column: coverage
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: average window depth, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Deepest window
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest window depth found, and the bars rank the libraries holding the deepest windows. It answers which library has the strongest pile-up.
    How to read: a maximum far above the median marks a collapsed region such as a repeat or an organelle contig. Open the track to see where it sits.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  column: coverage
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: deepest window, with the libraries that reach it ranked

- component: card
  title: Depth variability within windows
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average standard deviation of the depth inside a window, and the box shows how it varies between windows. It answers how uneven the depth is at a small scale.
    How to read: windows with a large deviation compared with their depth hold uneven or repetitive sequence. A library with a larger value overall is less uniform.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  column: coverage_std
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: average standard deviation of depth, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Depth per window
  description: |-
    Each row is a window of the reference with its contig, position, mean depth and the standard deviation of the depth inside it. It answers the exact depth behind the tracks.
    How to read: sort by depth to find the extreme windows, or filter by contig to inspect one sequence.
  page_size: 25

- component: advanced_viz
  id: depth_histogram_profile
  title: Share of the reference at each depth
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: the share of the reference sitting at each read depth. It answers how the depth is distributed over the genome, not only its mean.
    How to read: a curve with a tall left end means much of the reference is uncovered or shallow. A narrow peak near the mean depth means an even library and a long tail to the right means pile-ups on repeats. Compare libraries on the same curve before choosing which to resequence.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Read depth (X)
    y_title: Share of the reference
    log_y: true
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: coverage
    y: fraction

- component: figure
  title: Bases of the reference at each depth
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: the number of bases of the reference sitting at each read depth. It answers the same question as the share profile in raw base counts.
    How to read: raw counts depend on the reference size, so use this view for libraries mapped to the same reference and the share view otherwise. A large count at zero depth is the uncovered part of the genome.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: coverage
    y: n_genomic_locations
    color: sample
    labels:
      coverage: Read depth (X)
      n_genomic_locations: Bases of the reference
      sample: Library

- component: card
  title: Reference with no coverage
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of the reference with no read at all, and the bars rank the libraries with the largest uncovered share. It answers how much of the genome a library misses.
    How to read: a share near zero is a library that reaches the whole reference. A large share at zero depth is expected for a shallow library and is the first number to check before calling variants.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  column: fraction
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: col('coverage') == 0
  caption: median share at zero depth, with the least covered libraries ranked

- component: card
  title: Bases with no coverage
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest number of reference bases with no read, taken over the libraries. It answers how large the uncovered part is in bases rather than in share.
    How to read: compare the maximum with the lowest library to see how unequal the libraries are. Raw counts depend on the reference size, so read the share card for libraries on different references.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  column: n_genomic_locations
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: vertical
  filter_expr: col('coverage') == 0
  caption: median and lowest count of uncovered bases

- component: table
  title: Depth histogram
  description: |-
    Each row is a read depth of a library with the number of reference bases at that depth and their share of the reference. It answers the exact values behind the histogram.
    How to read: filter to one library and read down the depth column to find the depth that holds most of the genome.
  page_size: 25

- component: advanced_viz
  id: contig_depth_scatter
  title: Contig depth against contig length
  description: |-
    Each point is a contig in one library: its length on the horizontal axis and its depth relative to the library mean on the vertical axis, with the marker sized by the bases mapped to it. It answers whether any contig is over- or under-covered compared with the rest of the genome.
    How to read: most long contigs should sit near the mean. A short contig far above it is typically an organelle genome or a repeat, and a contig well below it may be a sex chromosome or a missing sequence. Compare libraries before reading a contig as a sex call.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is a relative depth of 1, the library's own genome-wide mean by definition. It is a data-defined reference, not a cut-off.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    log_x: true
    x_title: Contig length (bp)
    y_title: Depth relative to the library mean
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_value: 1
    reference_label: Library mean
    top_n_labels: 8
  roles:
    x: length
    y: relative_coverage
    label: chromosome
    color: sample
    size: mapped_bases

- component: figure
  title: Depth per contig, relative to the library mean
  description: |-
    Each bar is a contig in a library: its depth divided by the library's genome-wide mean. It answers which contigs deviate from the genome-wide level.
    How to read: a bar near 1 is a contig at the library mean. A bar far above or below it is worth a look, and an organelle contig is expected to tower over the rest.
    Lines and annotations: a relative depth of 1 is the library's own mean by definition, no cut-off is drawn.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: chromosome
    y: relative_coverage
    color: sample
    labels:
      chromosome: Contig
      relative_coverage: Depth relative to the library mean
      sample: Library

- component: card
  title: Relative contig depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median depth of a contig relative to its library mean, and the strip shows the lowest and highest contig. It answers how far the contigs depart from the genome-wide level.
    How to read: a median near 1 is expected. A maximum far above it points to an organelle genome or a repeat that took many reads.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  column: relative_coverage
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: vertical
  caption: median relative depth, with the lowest and highest contig

- component: card
  title: Bases mapped per contig
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of bases mapped, and the bars rank the contigs that hold most of them. It answers whether one scaffold soaked up the library.
    How to read: the ranking should follow contig length. A contig far above its share of the genome holds more reads than its size explains.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  column: mapped_bases
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: chromosome
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: total bases mapped, with the largest contigs ranked

- component: card
  title: Reference length by contig
  description: |-
    Each unit is a base of the reference and the ring splits them by contig. It answers how the reference is divided, to put the depth of each contig in context.
    How to read: a ring dominated by a few contigs means a chromosome-level assembly, and many thin slices mean a fragmented one.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  column: length
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  - median
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: chromosome
  caption: total length, split by contig

- component: table
  title: Per-contig depth
  description: |-
    Each row is a contig in a library with its length, mapped bases, mean depth, standard deviation and depth relative to the library mean. It answers the exact numbers behind the contig tiles.
    How to read: sort by relative depth to find the contigs that depart from the library mean.
  page_size: 25

- component: advanced_viz
  id: genome_fraction_profile
  title: Genome fraction covered at least X deep
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: the percentage of the reference covered by at least the read depth on the horizontal axis. It answers how much of the genome is usable at each depth, which a mean depth cannot tell.
    How to read: a curve that stays high as the depth rises is a library with its reads spread over the genome. A curve that collapses at the first depths means the reads are piled on a small part of it, so the mean depth overstates what is usable.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Minimum read depth (X)
    y_title: Reference covered (%)
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: min_coverage
    y: genome_fraction_pct

- component: figure
  title: Share of the reference covered at least X deep
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: the percentage of the reference covered at least X deep. It answers the same question as the profile as a plain line.
    How to read: compare where the curves reach the depth you need for your analysis, and read the gap between libraries as a difference in evenness.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: min_coverage
    y: genome_fraction_pct
    color: sample
    labels:
      min_coverage: Minimum read depth (X)
      genome_fraction_pct: Reference covered (%)
      sample: Library

- component: card
  title: Reference covered at 1X
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of the reference covered by at least one read, and the bars rank the libraries that cover most of it. It answers how complete a library is at the lowest depth.
    How to read: a low value means large parts of the genome are unseen. A library that is high here and drops quickly at higher depth is complete but shallow.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  column: genome_fraction_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: col('min_coverage') == 1
  caption: median percent covered by one read or more, with the best libraries ranked

- component: card
  title: Deepest depth still reached
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest depth at which some of the reference is still covered, and the bars rank the libraries that go deepest. It answers how far each library's curve extends.
    How to read: a short reach means a shallow library. The table is capped at the depths Qualimap reports, so a value at that cap means at least that deep.
    Source: http://qualimap.conesalab.org/doc_html/analysis.html
  column: min_coverage
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: col('genome_fraction_pct') > 0
  caption: highest depth with any coverage, with the libraries ranked

- component: table
  title: Genome fraction per depth
  description: |-
    Each row is a library at one minimum depth with the percentage of the reference covered at least that deep. It answers the exact values behind the curves.
    How to read: filter to a library and read down to the depth your analysis needs.
  page_size: 25
